The current bug report describes a discrepancy in the behavior of reading a ZIP file using commons-compress between version 1.6 and version 1.7. Specifically, when running the provided code snippet, it is observed that in commons-compress 1.6 the content of the test file "test.txt" is correctly read as "data\n", whereas in commons-compress 1.7 the content is read as "@@@@^@". 

By comparing the expected output "data\n" with the actual output "@@@@^@", it is evident that there is a problem with how the data is being read or processed in commons-compress 1.7. This suggests a potential issue with the handling of the ZIP archive entries or data in the newer version.

## Code Inspection
Looking at the test method `testReadingOfFirstStoredEntry` from `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStreamTest`, it opens a ZIP archive, reads the first entry, and performs assertions on the entry size and content.

The difference in output between commons-compress 1.6 and 1.7 implies a regression or a change in behavior in the handling of ZIP archive entries. Possible root causes could include:
1. Change in how ZIP archive entries are being processed or decoded in commons-compress 1.7.
2. Incorrect handling of character encoding or data interpretation in the newer version.

Further investigation into the implementation details of reading ZIP archive entries in commons-compress version 1.7 is necessary to pinpoint the exact source of the bug.
